heard: Ranger Ed Pulaski saved 40 men by holding them at gunpoint. In 1910, Hurricane Winds whipped Idaho into a three-million-acre firestorm. Smoke-blinded ships in the Pacific and turned midday into night. Trapped, Pulaski forced his panic crew into an abandoned mine tunnel. He drew his pistol, forcing them to stay until the firestorm passed. Today, wildland firefighters still honor his legacy with the tool named for him.
